use /lib
from /ui/components/inset-panel import InsetPanelScope
from /ui/components/scrollbar import ScrollbarScope

export scope DivergenceScope:
    concept: {DivergenceConcept}

concept DivergenceConcept:
    pitch:
        Shows how far the code and the spec have drifted apart: which parts of
        the spec drove each source file, and how strongly, what each side does
        that the other doesn't account for, and a single score for the whole
        project.

    shape: {DivergenceShape}

shape DivergenceShape:
    description:
        An analysis of the open project, shown in an @{InsetPanelScope} titled
        "Divergence", with a close button. Opening it starts a fresh analysis
        straight away. Closing the panel while it runs stops it. Once an
        analysis is over, an "Analyze again" button in the panel's header
        starts another.

    files:
        The source files are every file under the code location, codeRoot in
        piton.config.pi, leaving out what Git ignores and anything that isn't
        text. The spec files are every .pi file under the spec location, root in
        piton.config.pi. Paths are shown relative to the project. Each side is
        capped at 400 files, and the panel says when a side was cut short.

    analyzing:
        steps:
            The analysis first runs `piton build` in the project, so the
            compiled spec is up to date. A build that fails doesn't stop the
            analysis; the panel notes that the compiled spec may be out of
            date. Then two agents run at the same time: one analyzes the code,
            one analyzes the spec. While it runs, the panel lists the steps,
            "Building the spec", "Analyzing the code", and
            "Analyzing the spec", each with a spinner while it runs, a tick once
            done, or a cross and why if it failed.

        agents:
            Each agent is a one-off run of the harness in the project, which can
            only read, glob, and search files, never change anything, and keeps
            no session. It is given both lists of files, the code and spec
            locations, and that the compiled spec is in the agent directory's
            reference folder, and replies with nothing but JSON.

            The code agent goes through every source file, and for each says
            which spec files drove it or had influence on it, with how strong
            each influence is, from 0 for barely any to 1 for the file being
            written straight from it, and a short note on what it took from it;
            how far the file diverges from the spec, from 0 for doing just what
            the spec describes to 1 for nothing in the spec accounting for it or
            the spec saying otherwise; and a sentence summing up how it
            diverges, or that it doesn't.

            The spec agent goes through every spec file the same way from the
            other side: which source files implement it, and how strongly, how
            far the code diverges from what the file describes, from 0 for all
            of it being built as described to 1 for none of it being built or the
            code doing otherwise, and a sentence summing it up.

        failing:
            An agent that fails, or replies with something that can't be read,
            fails the analysis, and the panel says why. If only one agent
            fails, what the other found is still shown.

    results:
        connections:
            A connection joins a source file and a spec file. Its strength is
            the average of what both agents said of it, or what one said when
            only one mentioned it, from 0 to 1. Connections to files that aren't
            among the source or spec files are left out. A strength of two
            thirds or more is strong, one third or more moderate, and anything
            less weak.

        score:
            The divergence score is the average divergence of every file both
            agents analyzed, source and spec alike, as a whole percentage. A
            file an agent left out isn't counted, and is shown as
            "Not analyzed". The score is shown large in the header, with what
            it means beside it: "Aligned" below 20%, "Drifting" from 20% up to
            50%, and "Diverged" from 50%, coloured green, amber, and red.

        trees:
            Beneath the header, a switch between "Source" and "Spec" shows that
            side's files as a tree: a row per folder and file, indented by
            depth, folders before files, each sorted by name. A file's row
            shows its name, a small bar for its divergence, coloured as the
            score is, and its divergence as a percentage, or
            "Not analyzed". The tree scrolls with a @{ScrollbarScope}.

            Clicking a file selects it. Beside the tree, the selected file's
            details: its path, divergence, and summary, then its connections to
            files on the other side, strongest first, each with the other file's
            path, a bar as long as the connection is strong, its strength as a
            percentage, whether it is strong, moderate, or weak, and what the
            agents noted of it. Clicking a connection switches to the other
            tree with that file selected and scrolled into view. With nothing
            selected, the details say to select a file. When the analysis
            starts, the file with the highest divergence on the Source side is
            selected.
EOF

content.text:
I've added "Analyze Divergence" to the Spec tab, along with a new `DivergenceScope` in the spec. It opens an inset panel, runs the analysis, and shows a divergence score plus source and spec trees whose files link to each other by influence strength. I haven't run a real analysis end to end in the app. The tests use canned agent replies, and I only confirmed the agent command itself runs, with a tiny prompt.

**How the analysis runs:**
1. **Lists the files:** every text file under the code root (`codeRoot`, skipping Git-ignored files) and every `.pi` file under the spec root (`root`), capped at 400 per side.
2. **Builds the spec:** runs `piton build`. A failed build doesn't stop the analysis, but the panel notes the compiled spec may be out of date.
3. **Runs two agents in parallel**, each a one-off `claude -p` that can only read, glob and search files, and keeps no session. Both are given both file lists and reply with JSON only.
   - The code agent says, for each source file, which spec files influenced it and how strongly (0–1, with a note), how far it diverges (0–1), and a one-sentence summary.
   - The spec agent says the same from the other side: which source files implement each spec file and how strongly.
4. **Merges the replies:** each source–spec link gets the average strength of what the two agents said. Links to files outside the lists are dropped.
5. **Scores it:** the score is the average divergence of every file analyzed, as a percentage. Under 20% is Aligned (green), under 50% Drifting (amber), otherwise Diverged (red). Files an agent skipped show "Not analyzed" and don't count toward the score.

**The panel:**
- **While running:** each step shows a spinner, then a tick or a cross with the reason.
- **Header:** the score and its label, "Analyze again", and a close button. Closing while it runs kills both agent processes.
- **Trees:** a Source/Spec switch shows that side as a tree, with a divergence bar and percentage per file. The most divergent source file is selected to start.
- **Details:** the selected file's summary and its connections, strongest first. Each connection shows a strength bar, strong/moderate/weak, and the agents' notes. Clicking one jumps to that file in the other tree.
- **Partial failure:** if one agent fails, the other's results still show, with a note saying which failed.

**Before you run it:**
- **Cost:** the two agents use your default Claude model and may read many files, so a run on a big project will take a while and cost accordingly.
- **Results aren't saved:** closing the panel loses them.
- **Scores are estimates:** they're the agents' judgement, not a measured value, and may vary between runs.

**Tests:** the model tests cover:
- reading JSON with text around it;
- merging, averaging, dropping links to unknown files, and scoring;
- verdict and strength names, and building the tree;
- listing this repo's own files.

Two UI tests use canned agent replies. One checks the score, the initial selection, connection order and strength, following a connection into the Spec tree, and switching back. The other checks that a failed spec agent is marked failed while the code results still show.

The suite shows 149 passed, 1 skipped (it needs the real harness), and the same palette test failing as before. The build has no warnings.

**Spec:**
- **New `DivergenceScope`** (`spec/scope/divergence`): files, steps, agents, failures, connections, score, trees.
- **`RibbonSpecTabScope`:** a new Analysis group with the Analyze Divergence command.
- **`MainWindowScope`:** it opens in the inset panel.

`piton check` and `piton build check` pass, and I ran `piton build`.

**Code:**
- **New files:** `src/divergence.rs` (file listing, prompts, agent runner, merge, score, tree) and `src/divergence_view.rs` (the panel).
- **Command:** the ribbon button is in `src/ribbon/spec_tab.rs`.
- **Panel:** wired in `src/main_window.rs`.
